mnhs-markers.geojson.caveats: Hand-built, not a service pull. Coordinates are HMdb DMS converted to decimal degrees, per marker: the three Whipholt markers differ by metres within the parking area (Sugar Point Battle 47.050083, -94.357100; Gaa-zagaskwaajimekaag 47.050083, -94.357300; The Battle of Sugar Point 47.050117, -94.356883) — the brief's single coordinate 47.050083, -94.357100 is the Sugar Point Battle marker's coordinate. location_precision is 'marker site' throughout (parking area / museum frontage, not a surveyed point). Only the Sugar Point Battle plaque was erected by MNHS; the two newer Whipholt markers were erected by MnDOT and 'Stimulated Exploration' by the City of Walker (2015) — the latter is included per brief as the watershed's fur-trade marker at the Cass County Museum. MnDOT historic-roadsides list confirmation for the three Whipholt markers individually is still owed — OPEN CHECK, not confirmed here. (MnDOT does list the Whipholt Roadside Parking Area itself among its evaluated historic roadside properties, with an inventory form and a treatment report, and its project-selection list shows 'Whipholt 2020 Eligible' plus a 2023 small project 'Interpretation incomplete'; that confirms the site, not the three markers by name.) No MNHS-operated historic site exists in the watershed (HUC8 07010102) — no historic-sites layer was created; nearest MNHS sites outside the watershed are Forest History Center (Grand Rapids) and Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post (Onamia), context links only. Marker texts are transcribed verbatim from HMdb; no interpretive wording was added. The Battle of Sugar Point text carries an internal casualty discrepancy (opening: seven dead and ten wounded; later passage: six killed and ten wounded) versus the older plaque (7 killed and 16 wounded) — transcribed as written, not reconciled. HMdb's 'significant date' of October 5, 1869 on the Sugar Point Battle entry is an HMdb error (the battle was October 5, 1898) and was not carried into the file. Erection years for the three Whipholt markers are not stated on HMdb; recorded as null rather than guessed. Site rehabilitation completed 2020. THPO/Band: thpo_required is 'yes' on the three Whipholt markers; wording uses the Band's own text where it exists (Gaa-zagaskwaajimekaag text adapted from 'Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe: An Overview,' Leech Lake Tribal Development, 2022). The Gaa-zagaskwaajimekaag display's additional panels (Official Emblem, Manoomin/Wild Rice, Story of the Seven Fires, reservation map, historic images) are not transcribed in marker_text. The Circle of Time monument has 13 markers; only 'Stimulated Exploration' is in this layer.
mnhs-markers.geojson.query: Hand-built point layer — no pull service exists. Four HMdb entries verified 2026-11-21: Sugar Point Battle (m=124726), Gaa-zagaskwaajimekaag (m=266795), The Battle of Sugar Point (m=266796), "Stimulated Exploration" (m=235799); coordinates converted from HMdb DMS. MnDOT historic-roadsides pages checked for the Whipholt site (dot.state.mn.us/roadsides/historic).
